description:
Space-agency and operator photos on /credits are grouped under the 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' section instead of under their actual agency's section (e.g. CMSA/China Manned Space Agency photos — 135 entries — appear under Wikimedia Commons; SpaceIL photos under Wikimedia Commons; USAF photos under Wikimedia Commons; CSA photos under Wikimedia Commons despite a CSA source-logo existing)

Expected: Each photo on /credits should be grouped under its producing agency's source-logo section. The governing editorial rule is documented in the comment above `agencyToSourceId` in `src/lib/credits-grouping.ts` (lines ~162-172): the upstream publisher (the agency that flew the hardware / produced the image) wins over the retrieval conduit (Wikimedia Commons). A photo of a Chang'e lander retrieved via Commons must appear in the CNSA section, not the Commons section.

Acceptance criteria:
- Entries with agency='CMSA' are grouped under a source section (either an existing CNSA section or a new CMSA section) instead of under 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' [spec: src/lib/credits-grouping.ts, `agencyToSourceId`, the docstring at lines ~162-172: 'the upstream publisher wins over the retrieval conduit']
- Entries with agency='SpaceIL' are grouped under a SpaceIL source section instead of under 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' [spec: Same docstring — SpaceIL is the operator that produced Beresheet imagery, Commons is only the conduit]
- Entries with agency='USAF' are grouped under a USAF or related section instead of under 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' [spec: Same docstring]
- Entries with agency='CSA' (Canadian Space Agency, e.g. Canadarm2) are grouped under the existing 'csa' source-logo section instead of under 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' [repo-data: static/data/source-logos.json has a CSA entry (id='csa', kind='space-agency') already registered; agencyToSourceId should route to it]
- Entries with agency='USSR Post' are grouped under a Roscosmos/Soviet section instead of under 'Wikimedia Commons contributors' [reporter: These are Soviet space probe images (e.g. Mars 2 orbiter); the operator is the Soviet space program (Roscosmos predecessor)]

Domain facts:
- CMSA (China Manned Space Agency) is distinct from CNSA (China National Space Administration). Both are Chinese space agencies. Maintainer decision needed: add 'cmsa' source-logo entry or route CMSA to the existing 'cnsa' source.
- SpaceIL is an Israeli non-profit that built the Beresheet lander. No source-logo entry exists.
- USAF (U.S. Air Force) is distinct from USSF (U.S. Space Force) and NASA. No source-logo entry exists for USAF; operator of the X-37B OTV missions.
- CSA (Canadian Space Agency) has a source-logo entry (id='csa') but agencyToSourceId doesn't check for 'csa' or 'canadian space agency'.
